summaries.body:
The 5.0 mapping records V16.3.1 as modified and moved from 4.0.3 V7.2.1, which asked that all authentication decisions be logged without storing sensitive session tokens or passwords, including requests with metadata needed for investigations. The current clause logs all authentication operations, successful and unsuccessful, plus extra metadata such as authentication type or factors. The mapping notes predecessor text is dissimilar and git diverges from the ID slot; mapping and V7.2.1 wording are still the reliable origin.

Abhay's 10 February 2019 CWE pass records V7.2.1. Andrew van der Stock updated V7 CWE items on 20 February 2019. Elar Lang's 18 March 2021 commit 3f555fd3 closed #862 (moving log-related parts of V14.5.1 toward the log category); Jim Manico had asked in that issue to drop logging from the HTTP-methods control and keep a generic access-control-failure log instead. Grammarly and session-chapter file stamps on V7.2.1 are not origin.

On 2 June 2020 Josh Grossman changed "session identifier" to "session token" on V7.2.1 (661b05a8). 5.0 then dropped the "without storing tokens or passwords" clause from this ID (that concern lives with V16.2.5) and added successful/unsuccessful attempts plus factor metadata. #643 (CSP acronym) and session-management file updates stamped on V7.2.1 are not wording changes to this authentication-logging control. Skip Grammarly and spacing-only commits.
